completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: Canal de São Gonçalo opening into Lagoa dos Patos beside Pelotas.
completion_scope.ordinary_scale_note: Correspondence is at generalized river, tributary, wetland-connector and lake-passage scale. It does not demand agreement with each bank, bend, headmost vertex or exact surveyed mouth point. Small unnamed openings are geographically covered without a name assignment.

records.region: Uruguay and southern Brazil; selected transboundary lagoon and tributary setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative downstream conduit/system identity only; no uniform whole-feature hydronym.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected mainstem follows a small headward opening into Arroio Basílio, then Rio Piratini and Canal São Gonçalo to Lagoa dos Patos. Its tributary selection includes separate Uruguay river corridors, Jaguarão and extensive Lagoa Mirim/Merín passages. Original cartography provides positive correspondence for all 22 selected fragments. Canal São Gonçalo is retained only as the representative downstream identity.
records.supported_name_scope: Downstream representative identity spanning a selected compound river–lagoon group.

component_scope_limits: Canal São Gonçalo is a representative downstream name. It is not the uniform name of Arroio Basílio, Rio Piratini, the Uruguay branches, Jaguarão, or the Lagoa Mirim/Merín lake passages.
Unlabelled small headward streams remain null. Names read from bounded source features are not promoted to accepted full-fragment names.
Cebollatí, Olimar Grande, Tacuarí, San Luis and Jaguarão are distinguished as separate river corridors; in-lagoon model joins are not asserted to be ordinary river confluences.
The selected opening east of the India Muerta reservoir is not automatically a reservoir passage merely because that reservoir lies nearby.
The stored sea terminal class does not establish an Atlantic mouth; the actual depicted terminal is Lagoa dos Patos.
Neither present-day flow direction at every lake/channel reach nor hydraulic control operations, official hydronym limits or registry status is established.

records.completion_scope: All of the sole selected FID was considered against the original full-corridor map and detailed Talagapa original. The mapped corridor and terminal are established at ordinary geographic scale; no precise bank, source-tip or surveyed mouth match is required. The remaining issue is the extended upland approach and its connection to the first mapped intermittent feeder, not a small terminal-vertex discrepancy.
records.region: Chubut, Patagonia, Argentina; selected inland drainage toward the Telsen region.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional candidate from the independently mapped named middle/lower receiving corridor. Whole-object representative identity remains unestablished because the extreme western Talagapa headward connection is unresolved. Cañadón Largo is a separately mapped valley name, not a scalar hydronym for the entire line.
records.material_pending_reason: The extended eastern Talagapa upland opening and its connection into the first mapped intermittent feeder west of Puesto Betelo remain unestablished. The visible feeder, Cañadón Largo, Arroyo Telsen and terminal wet depression are mapped, but do not close this headward interval.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Original IGN cartography establishes the visible intermittent feeder near Puesto Betelo, the eastward Cañadón Largo corridor and its junction at Las Horquetas, the named Arroyo Telsen through Chacras de Telsen, Telsen and Chasicó, and the actual selected terminal within an unnamed shallow wet depression in Bajo de la Tierra Colorada. The extended western opening on the eastern Talagapa upland is not independently connected to the printed feeder by the inspected sources. This is material-source pending, not a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional candidate from the independently mapped named middle/lower receiving corridor. Whole-object representative identity remains unestablished because the extreme western Talagapa headward connection is unresolved. Cañadón Largo is a separately mapped valley name, not a scalar hydronym for the entire line.

component_scope_limits: Arroyo Telsen is a provisional named middle/lower-corridor candidate while material headward correspondence remains incomplete.
The western upland opening and printed Betelo feeder have null hydronyms in this finding.
Cañadón Largo and Cañadón Chileno are mapped valley/drainage names; neither is automatically a scalar hydronym for the whole selected line.
Northern and western neighboring lakes and tributaries are not traversed merely because they drain toward the named river.
The selected terminal is an unnamed wet depression in Bajo de la Tierra Colorada; the basin name does not identify a uniformly named lake or river.
Historical cartography does not establish current perennial flow, modern works, exact banks, individual naming-transition vertices or formal registry status.
Accepted, whole-feature scalar and Korean names remain null; every application flag is false.

material_pending_components.component: Extended eastern Talagapa upland opening to the printed feeder west of Puesto Betelo
material_pending_components.needed_evidence: Independent original mapping or bounded primary evidence establishing the entire selected opening and its connection to the first mapped intermittent feeder. The present terrain contours, basin context and model connectivity do not independently supply that connection.

records.region: Northeastern Florida and southeastern Georgia, United States.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative downstream river-system candidate; supported for the mapped North Prong and St. Marys corridor, not a completed identity of the whole selected object.
records.material_pending_reason: The initial opening south of Horse Shoe Break and the northwest traverse through the southeastern Okefenokee wetland to the mapped North Prong remain unestablished as a connected waterway. The downstream St. Marys corridor and southern Cumberland Sound terminal are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Readable primary cartography establishes the selected North Prong Saint Marys River and St. Marys River corridor from the southern Okefenokee margin through the main tributary junctions and Folkston bend to the tidal mouth in southern Cumberland Sound. The initial selected opening south of Horse Shoe Break and its northwest traverse through the southeastern Okefenokee wetland are not established as a connected waterway by the acquired maps. This is a genuine headward/connector evidence gap, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.completion_scope: Readable primary cartography establishes the selected North Prong Saint Marys River and St. Marys River corridor from the southern Okefenokee margin through the main tributary junctions and Folkston bend to the tidal mouth in southern Cumberland Sound. The initial selected opening south of Horse Shoe Break and its northwest traverse through the southeastern Okefenokee wetland are not established as a connected waterway by the acquired maps. This is a genuine headward/connector evidence gap, not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional representative downstream river-system candidate; supported for the mapped North Prong and St. Marys corridor, not a completed identity of the whole selected object.

component_scope_limits: Saint Marys River is the spelling visible on USGSTopo; St. Marys River is used by the NPS report and SJRWMD page. Neither spelling is assigned to the full selected object.

North Prong Saint Marys River is a distinguishable mapped upstream component. Middle Prong, South Prong, Cedar Creek and other lateral tributaries are not renamed after the representative downstream river.
The initial selected feeder and its northwest cross-swamp connection remain unnamed and unestablished. The Okefenokee place label and basin association alone do not establish their correspondence.
Nearby Bee Gum Lake, Coward Lake and mapped swamp ponds are contextual features. No selected passage through either named lake is established.

The retained terminal class is sea, but the observed selected endpoint is at the river's entry to southern Cumberland Sound, west of the ocean inlet; it is not extended to an Atlantic shoreline mouth point.

records.supported_name_scope: Context only: Taserssuaq/Tasersuaq identifies the lower lake; Tasersiaq is a distinct southern lake; Nivingmaneq locates the lower valley; Umiviit and Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord identify the receiving marine setting. No label is applied uniformly to FID 8876.

completion_scope.scale: Ordinary generalized geographic corridor/component scale. No exact bank, vertex, lake shoreline, glacier-front or mouth-point agreement is asserted or required.
completion_scope.hydrological_continuity_claim: No assertion that the interior ice/rock model course is a surveyed continuous surface or subglacial river. Geographic completion is distinct from hydrological or scalar-name proof.

records.region: Western Greenland; selected inland-to-coastal ice, rock and valley setting.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The complete selected geographic setting is accounted for by adjoining original maps: interior ice, ice-margin and rock terrain, lower lake passage, deposit-filled northern connector and receiving fjord arm. No single natural-river hydronym is established across those different components. This is a naming-scope limitation, not missing source or connector coverage.
records.geographic_disambiguation: FID 8876 begins in the Inland Ice east of Tasersiaq, bends north and east, turns west into the exposed-rock belt north of that lake, returns northeast and then northwest, and reaches the southern Tasersuaq lake setting. Its lower westward passage and northward exit are covered across the join of GEUS Sheets 2 and 3. The ending occupies the sediment-filled lower valley at the Umiviit arm of Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord, south of the separate town-head outlet beside Kangerlussuaq. Original cartography accounts for the full setting without establishing one natural river or a whole-route river name.

component_scope_limits: Context only: Taserssuaq/Tasersuaq identifies the lower lake; Tasersiaq is a distinct southern lake; Nivingmaneq locates the lower valley; Umiviit and Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord identify the receiving marine setting. No label is applied uniformly to FID 8876.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
